behavior: Saving billing details needs a fresh sign-in, and Sign out everywhere ends every session
acceptance: PUT billing-details needs a token at most 5 minutes old whose iat equals the latest_verified_at of the user's email or passkey account at Privy; otherwise 401 reauth_required and nothing is saved; a Privy failure saves nothing

Every signed-in route refuses a token issued before the user's sessions_revoked_at with 401; POST /v1/me/sign-out-everywhere freezes and unfreezes the user at Privy, then sets it; a failed freeze sets nothing, the unfreeze is always sent, and a failed unfreeze still sets it

On reauth_required the web opens a dialog that sends a code to the login email, signs in again and repeats the request with the new token; Cancel leaves it unsaved; a user with no email login is told so
The account menu offers Sign out everywhere behind a confirm dialog and signs out; axe finds 0 serious or critical violations on both dialogs
R-137, api.md, openapi.yaml and the architecture docs describe it; required checks and a11y-e2e pass
notes: 2026-10-24 review fail by reviewer: BLOCKING 1: apps/backend/internal/privy/privy.go:101-111 EndSessions sends the freeze on the request context. If the client disconnects (closes the tab) or the SDK times out while the freeze is in flight, Privy may have frozen the user, but the function returns before the unfreeze. The comment says the unfreeze runs even if the caller gives up, which is false for this phase. Request contexts do get canceled here: the e2e log shows 'context canceled' errors. A retry then starts with Freeze on a user who is already frozen, and that case is not measured; if Privy refuses it, the unfreeze never runs again. The user is then locked out with no self-service way back. Fix: run EndSessions and the UPDATE in profile/sessions.go:15 on context.WithoutCancel, and send the unfreeze whenever a freeze was sent, even when the freeze failed. Add a test for an unfreeze failure: the fake's FailFreezes fails only POST. BLOCKING 2: docs/PROJECT.md:189 R-137, and accept 2, say sign-out-everywhere 'sets it, then freezes and unfreezes'. The code and api.md do Privy first, then the cutoff. The written order is the unsafe one: on a Privy failure the user is cut off, but the attacker's refresh tokens live and give post-cutoff tokens. Fix the row and the accept line. NON-BLOCKING: (a) profile/sessions.go:15 date_trunc plus auth/service.go:24 strict > let a token issued in the cutoff second, before the freeze, pass. Hard to exploit, but dropping date_trunc closes it at no cost. (b) httpapi/tests/auth_test.go:71 signedInAt is fixed at package init, so every billing PUT in the package fails once it has run 5 minutes. It runs about 61s now; -count=5 or a slow CI breaks it. (c) Test gaps: other account types (google_oauth, wallet) not shown to be ignored; the dialog's Cancel resolving false is untested, and a broken onClose would hang the save; no test that a second reauth_required is not asked again. (d) apps/web/e2e/privy/navigation.spec.ts:911: the reasoning holds (workers 1, file order, the next test mocks logout and the API). But the state is saved only at the end, so a failure after the re-sign-in leaves later tests on the replaced session; save it right after the dialog closes. Both API answers are mocked, so the real iat = latest_verified_at match rests on S-8 only. (e) mid/auth.go:29 CheckSession queries the DB before the rate limit, one query per flooded request; acceptable trade-off, worth knowing. (f) account-menu.tsx:34/121 the mutation's isError persists, so reopening the dialog shows the old error. (g) D-49 limit: a stolen session can link its own passkey at Privy, sign in with it and pass the fresh check; record it for D-49/F294. (h) docs/backend/api.md:555 the Guards list does not name FreshSignIn. Checked fine: guard order (user, cutoff, limit, owner, then Privy), every signed-in route goes through the guards, missing iat reads as epoch, a Privy failure gives 500 with nothing saved, logs hold only the route and the DID, web retry once with one shared dialog, public stores have no freshSignIn, kit Dialog onClose, the auth-api placement, doc sentence lengths. Backend tests TestBillingDetailsNeedAFreshSignIn and TestSignOutEverywhere pass; vitest src/shared/api and src/providers: 12 pass.

2026-10-24 review pass by reviewer: Re-review of the delta. Both blocking findings are fixed. (1) privy.go EndSessions runs on context.WithoutCancel, gives each call its own timeout and always sends the unfreeze. profile/sessions.go sets the cutoff only after a freeze that worked, also on WithoutCancel. TestSignOutEverywhere covers a failed freeze (unfreeze sent last, session kept) and a failed unfreeze (500, older token 401). The fake records failed calls and has FailUnfreezes. (2) R-137, accept 2, api.md and openapi.yaml give the code's order: freeze and unfreeze, then the cutoff. The earlier notes are addressed. The cutoff is now() with no date_trunc. signedInAt is set per invoiceAPI, and no test runs in parallel. There are tests for Google not counting, for a second reauth_required being the answer, and for Cancel in the live test. The live test saves the session right after the dialog closes. The menu dialog resets on close. Q-13 records the passkey-linking gap, and the api.md guards list names FreshSignIn. NON-BLOCKING: after a freeze that worked, a failed unfreeze (after the SDK's retries) still locks the user out. The cutoff now refuses their own token, so Try again in the dialog answers 401, and a frozen user can't sign in. Recovery is by hand at Privy, from the error log line that names the DID. This trade-off is chosen and documented. Consider an alert or a later retry. Ran: go test -race on TestBillingDetailsNeedAFreshSignIn, TestSignOutEverywhere, TestBusinessInvoiceNeedsBillingDetails and TestProfileRoutes*: ok. vitest src/shared/api and src/providers: 13 pass.
